Inspect the appropriate installation step, description, defaults, permitted values/range and error feedback; exercise each supported option, then restore the initial setting.

Verify successful installation, exact candidate GUID/version, selected room assignment and stable managed-child identities against the configuration API and app. Commission each child through the actual initial configuration step even when it has no prompts. Repeated state reads must preserve its controller identity and readiness; successful reconnect must recover existing children, while failed reads must not falsely revive them. Reopen Installer settings after connection and reload; confirm the previously supplied value, using private masked comparison for secrets.

Open this page from each supported entry point; close/back returns to the correct Home/room or parent page without sending a device command or saving uncommitted edits.

Cause each supported state change independently on the test hub; compare gateway/thermostat tile status and icon with the observed device state. Record response latency against an explicitly reviewed prompt-feedback budget and restore state.
Physically remove the isolated hub connection/power, timestamp that event, and verify every affected tile reports offline within 15 seconds. Preserve captures and independent disconnection timing.

Restore the isolated hub connection; timestamp first independently observed communication and the tile recovery. Verify valid current state and recovery latency against the reviewed prompt-feedback budget.

Compare the final candidate definition/localization with this rendered target. Exercise all visibility/enabled variants, error states and conditional schedule slots. Record the complete observed inventory; source parsing alone is insufficient.

Inspect the final candidate definitions and all runtime/configuration variants. Record NotApplicable with retained absence evidence only if no segmented-sliders exist. A framework-generated control or new definition invalidates this absence proposal.

Check name/status, operate both transitions repeatedly and rapidly, observe independent device state after each accepted action, and verify UI/device agreement. Busy disabling must not leave stale state; restore the full initial state.

Verify label, status and repeated intended response. Exercise each defined busy/disabled/error condition for its full duration and recovery; compare device feedback. For undeclared alert behavior record explicit absence evidence rather than inventing an alert.

Inspect the final candidate definitions and all runtime/configuration variants. Record NotApplicable with retained absence evidence only if no toggle-sliders exist. A framework-generated control or new definition invalidates this absence proposal.

Inspect the framework-rendered thermostat gauge, defined labels and supported bounds; independently vary reported temperature and verify display/feedback. Do not exempt native-rendered gauges solely because the XML tag is thermostat.

Verify label/icon and repeated operation of this button, with independent command/state evidence and measured feedback. Save Day and Save All must use isolated schedules; verify intended scope and restore all affected shared schedules/rooms.

Retain a pending edit across repeated successful polling, independently change the shared schedule or room assignment, then attempt Save Day/Save All. The newer hub data must survive, pending fields must remain, and the complete recovery instruction must be readable. Cancel/reopen must show current hub data. Also exercise failed pre-save reads, rejected writes and failed/mismatching post-save confirmation without reporting success. Restore all schedules and room settings.

For a room without an assignment, entering Auto requires an accepted and independently confirmed schedule assignment first. Rejected, unconfirmed or missing assignments must leave mode unchanged. Exercise existing manual targets equal to and different from current target, and the missing-manual-target variant only under its explicit initialization/restoration policy. Restore original mode, targets and assignment; report any retained inactive initialized value rather than claiming exact restoration.
Capture grouping, order and spacing in every visibility variant; all members must remain visually grouped and usable.

Verify labels and every supported choice. Capture the complete choice inventory and each selection result. Day/time changes affect the editor until save; schedule selection changes the assignment. Verify those intended semantics and restore original editor/hub state.

On an isolated, explicitly bound test schedule, verify that changed hub schedule labels and available choices are republished to the already-open Home selector without reloading the driver. Verify the selected ID remains correctly associated with its label, unchanged lists do not disrupt selection, and unavailable/deleted choices cannot assign an unintended schedule. Independently verify hub assignment and restore all affected schedule definitions and room assignments. Initial list inspection alone does not satisfy this check.

A selected schedule is published only after acceptance and fresh independent hub confirmation of the assigned ID. Exercise rejected assignment, failed read-back, and an unavailable/deleted ID; retain error and pending/observed UI state. No command is automatically replayed. Restore every affected assignment and schedule.

Retain at least 24 hours of periodic functional observations of the same connected Release candidate. The read-only sampling plan must be reviewed before collection and exercise actual driver/device feedback, not reachability alone. Bind the installed payload, driver lifetime, processor boot identity and successful hub-refresh marker to the candidate; verify current independent hub feedback and retain sample timing and gaps. After the retained 24-hour observation period, verify the same unchanged candidate is still connected and every applicable gateway, room, native thermostat and schedule function works. Bind these tests to the collected package and instance, record their real start/end times after the collection's last sample, and account for every applicable function using the reviewed acceptance coverage and actual test results. The collection timer or read-only feedback alone cannot satisfy this scope; do not extend the periodic sample interval to include these later tests.

Review actual pre-period, periodic and post-period observations for the unchanged candidate and confirm no performance degradation: commands remain prompt and independent physical/UI feedback remains accurate and prompt. Name the compared functions, operating conditions, baseline evidence, trigger/response definitions and reviewed acceptance budgets. Use measured command-to-observed-response intervals, excluding later screenshot/navigation work; a test's total elapsed time is not a command latency. Compare retained values rather than declaring success from a passing count, connection flag or elapsed duration. Account explicitly for missing or incomparable baseline measurements; they cannot support an unqualified no-degradation claim. This review performs no new device action; any new measurement must use the separately restored control-test scope.
